atlas_studies.author: Boissy et al.
atlas_studies.title: DeoxyArbutin: a novel reversible tyrosinase inhibitor with effective in vivo skin lightening potency
atlas_studies.design: Human treatment study with preclinical experiments
atlas_studies.population: Light- and dark-skinned participants; study also reports in vitro and animal experiments
atlas_studies.endpoint: Overall skin lightness and solar lentigines
atlas_studies.finding: Human treatment produced a significant or slight improvement in skin lightness/lentigines in light- and dark-skinned groups respectively, as phrased in the abstract. The exact subgroup statistical comparison requires full-text verification.
atlas_studies.insight: Apparent variation in response supports testing the same inhibitor across measured melanin levels, rather than extrapolating animal activity.
atlas_studies.limitations: Small subgroup sizes have been reported secondarily; primary abstract gives no subgroup denominators, and a formal between-group effect estimate was not confirmed.
atlas_studies.flags: Preclinical data; no confirmed interaction test; possible subgroup imprecision

atlas_studies.author: Berardesca & Maibach
atlas_studies.title: Racial differences in sodium lauryl sulphate induced cutaneous irritation: black and white
atlas_studies.population: Nine White and ten Black male volunteers
atlas_studies.duration: Patch test; exposure duration not confirmed in abstract
atlas_studies.endpoint: TEWL, laser Doppler blood flow, stratum corneum water content
atlas_studies.finding: SLS at 0.5% and 2% produced differences in barrier and erythematous responses depending on skin group and pretreatment site; the pattern was not a simple universal increase in sensitivity in one group.
atlas_studies.insight: Evaluate cleanser exposure and irritation using both barrier measurements and clinical signs in a diverse sample.
atlas_studies.limitations: Very small all-male sample; group labels are not quantitative melanin measurement; patch test is not a finished-product use trial.
atlas_studies.flags: Small sample; race as proxy; irritation challenge is not cosmetic efficacy

atlas_studies.author: Czernielewski et al.
atlas_studies.title: Efficacy and cutaneous safety of adapalene in black patients versus white patients with acne vulgaris
atlas_studies.population: Black and White patients treated for acne
atlas_studies.endpoint: Acne lesion reduction; dryness and skin tolerability
atlas_studies.finding: Acne efficacy was broadly similar across groups. Published analysis reported fewer moderate-to-severe dryness events among Black patients; specific percentages should be checked in the full paper before reuse.
atlas_studies.insight: Separately analyse efficacy and tolerability; neither can be inferred from pigmentation alone.
atlas_studies.limitations: Pooled subgroup analysis; formulations and treatment regimens specific to adapalene 0.1% gel; population labels are not phototype readings.
atlas_studies.flags: Meta-analysis subgroup; do not generalize to all retinoids
atlas_studies.status: PubMed record and publisher excerpt checked

atlas_studies.author: Talwar et al.
atlas_studies.title: Differential regulation of tyrosinase activity in skin of white and black individuals in vivo by topical retinoic acid
atlas_studies.finding: Short exposure increased measured tyrosinase activity in White skin but not Black skin under the reported experimental conditions.
atlas_studies.insight: The same retinoid can yield different short-term biochemical responses across populations; distinguish mechanistic markers from clinical pigmentation outcomes.
atlas_studies.limitations: Short-term mechanistic response, not a long-term hyperpigmentation efficacy comparison; no basis to conclude tretinoin is ineffective in darker skin.
atlas_studies.flags: Biochemical surrogate endpoint; not clinical efficacy
atlas_studies.status: PubMed indexing and publisher excerpt checked

atlas_studies.author: Tsai et al.
atlas_studies.title: Effects of glycolic acid on light-induced skin pigmentation in Asian and Caucasian subjects
atlas_studies.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology
atlas_studies.population: Asian and Caucasian volunteers with overlapping phototypes
atlas_studies.phototypes: Reported as II-IV across cohorts in secondary summary; verify against full text
atlas_studies.n: 12 (reported in earlier summary; confirm in full text)
atlas_studies.endpoint: UV-induced tanning and resolution of pre-existing pigmentation
atlas_studies.finding: The investigation reported altered tanning responses following glycolic acid pretreatment, rather than proof that glycolic acid uniformly prevents pigmentation.
atlas_studies.insight: Exfoliation studies should include UV-exposure context, irritation and pigmentation follow-up when targeting PIH-prone users.
atlas_studies.limitations: Small study; phototype overlap and ethnic group labels confound a pigmentation-specific explanation; no generalized clinical recommendation.
atlas_studies.flags: Small sample; exposure paradigm; phototype/ethnicity overlap
atlas_studies.status: PubMed indexing and publisher abstract checked

atlas_studies.author: Lee et al.
atlas_studies.title: Ethnic differences in objective and subjective skin irritation response: an international study
atlas_studies.ingredients: Sodium lauryl sulfate 0.5%; retinol 0.15%; lactic acid 5%; capsaicin 0.001%
atlas_studies.population: Asian and Caucasian participants in four countries
atlas_studies.phototypes: Not defined by melanin index in abstract
atlas_studies.endpoint: Irritation scores, positive patch reactions and self-reported stinging
atlas_studies.finding: Asian participants scored higher for SLS irritation, showed greater lactic-acid stinging and tended toward more positive retinol reactions; self-perceived sensitivity was similar.
atlas_studies.insight: Use both observer-rated irritation and participant-reported stinging in multicultural tolerability studies.
atlas_studies.limitations: Ethnicity is not synonymous with skin pigmentation; provocation tests do not establish performance of leave-on finished products.
atlas_studies.flags: Ethnicity confounding; standardized irritants not market formulations

atlas_studies.author: Racial differences cohort study authors
atlas_studies.title: Racial differences in tolerability of topical retinoids: A 15-year single-center retrospective cohort study
atlas_studies.population: White, Black and Asian adult patients prescribed retinoids for acne
atlas_studies.finding: Tolerability patterns differed by recorded race/ethnicity; Black patients had lower adjusted odds of intolerance than Asian patients in this cohort.
atlas_studies.insight: Design prospective tolerability assessments with carefully measured skin pigmentation, treatment exposures and follow-up.
atlas_studies.limitations: Single-centre retrospective medical records; 21.4% lost to follow-up as reported in full text; residual confounding; race not melanin index.
atlas_studies.flags: Observational; selection and reporting bias; no causal attribution
atlas_studies.status: PubMed record and open-access article checked

atlas_studies.author: Berardesca & Maibach
atlas_studies.title: Sodium-lauryl-sulphate-induced cutaneous irritation. Comparison of white and Hispanic subjects
atlas_studies.phototypes: Not reported as quantitative pigmentation in abstract
atlas_studies.endpoint: TEWL, stratum corneum water content and cutaneous blood flow
atlas_studies.finding: TEWL and water-content responses were greater in Hispanic participants, while measured microcirculatory responses were similar between groups.
atlas_studies.insight: Separate barrier response from vascular response when measuring irritation, and avoid ethnicity-based blanket claims.
atlas_studies.limitations: Hispanic is an ethnic category covering many pigment levels; small historical irritant study.
atlas_studies.flags: Ethnicity as proxy; short irritation challenge

atlas_studies.author: Dumbuya et al.
atlas_studies.title: Impact of Iron-Oxide Containing Formulations Against Visible Light-Induced Skin Pigmentation in Skin of Color Individuals
atlas_studies.ingredients: Iron oxides; zinc oxide; titanium dioxide
atlas_studies.finding: Iron-oxide-containing test formulations reduced induced pigmentation compared with untreated skin and the tested mineral SPF 50+ formula lacking iron oxides.
atlas_studies.insight: Measure visible-light coverage in addition to UV SPF when developing pigmentation-oriented tinted sunscreens.
atlas_studies.limitations: One phototype and specific tested products; sunscreen SPF alone does not measure visible-light attenuation; do not infer all iron-oxide formulas perform equally.
atlas_studies.flags: Product-specific result; may involve industry-sponsored products

atlas_studies.author: Grimes et al.
atlas_studies.title: Photoprotection Efficacy of Sun Protection Factor and Iron Oxide Formulations in Diverse Skin With Melasma and Photodamage
atlas_studies.population: Women with Fitzpatrick III–VI, including melasma subgroup
atlas_studies.endpoint: Clinical appearance and L* colour measurements
atlas_studies.finding: Both routines improved appearance over baseline; at 12 weeks, 36% of melasma participants in the SPF 50 + iron-oxide group met the reported superior improvement in L* versus 0% in SPF 50 alone.
atlas_studies.insight: Compare broad-spectrum UV protection alone versus combined UV and visible-light photoprotection for pigmentation outcomes.
atlas_studies.limitations: Product/regimen rather than isolated ingredient comparison; the 36% figure applies to a particular study endpoint and subgroup, not a general cure rate.

atlas_studies.author: Piffaut et al.
atlas_studies.title: Topical prevention from high energy visible light-induced pigmentation by 2-mercaptonicotinoyl glycine, but not by ascorbic acid antioxidant: 2 randomized controlled trials
atlas_studies.population: 58 Fitzpatrick III–IV individuals across two studies
atlas_studies.finding: 2-MNG reduced visible-light-induced pigmentation under trial conditions; topical 7% ascorbic acid did not demonstrate the same preventive outcome relative to control.
atlas_studies.insight: Match a proposed antioxidant claim to the causal stimulus and endpoint; UV-related and visible-light-related pigmentation are not interchangeable.
atlas_studies.limitations: Does not test treatment of existing spots or establish failure of vitamin C for other uses; limited to phototypes III–IV and study vehicles.
atlas_studies.flags: Specific light source and endpoint; cannot extrapolate to general vitamin C efficacy

atlas_studies.author: Liyanage et al.
atlas_studies.title: Comparative Study on Depigmenting Agents in Skin of Color
atlas_studies.journal: Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology
atlas_studies.ingredients: Arbutin 5%; azelaic acid 20%; hydroquinone 4%; resveratrol 1%; ascorbyl palmitate 1%
atlas_studies.population: Two groups of healthy Sri Lankan female volunteers
atlas_studies.endpoint: Mexameter melanin index relative to controls
atlas_studies.finding: Within single-active lipophilic dispersions, only 5% arbutin was significantly different from the inactive control; some commercial products also outperformed untreated sites.
atlas_studies.insight: Control for vehicle and exposure before claiming a depigmenting ingredient is superior.
atlas_studies.limitations: Small single-centre short study; separate phases; does not prove universal ingredient ranking or establish general treatment guidance.

atlas_studies.author: Roggenkamp et al.
atlas_studies.title: Effective reduction of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation with the tyrosinase inhibitor isobutylamido-thiazolyl-resorcinol (Thiamidol)
atlas_studies.comparison: Treatment vs vehicle within darker phototypes
atlas_studies.population: Dark-skinned volunteers with experimentally induced or acne-associated PIH
atlas_studies.phototypes: V and VI cohorts reported in full text
atlas_studies.endpoint: PIH lesion visibility, melanin index and clinical grading
atlas_studies.finding: Thiamidol-containing products improved suction-blister and acne-related PIH endpoints over vehicle or baseline under the study conditions.
atlas_studies.insight: Distinguish improvement in existing PIH from prevention of newly induced PIH; track both lesion and surrounding-skin colour.
atlas_studies.limitations: Several authors employed by the product manufacturer; patented ingredient; selected formulations and phototypes, not a universal comparative response.
atlas_studies.flags: Industry conflicts of interest; multiple different sub-studies
